items.title: Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Upends Plans and Adds Costs for Marching Bands
items.summary: Nine marching bands were set to perform in the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade. The decision to move the event to Saturday posed new logistical challenges for them.

items.title: Thanksgiving Parade Balloons Are Deflated in New York
items.summary: After the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade was postponed because of a powerful storm, crews worked through the night to deflate balloons before the bad weather arrived.

items.title: The Army Knew Much Earlier of the Explosive Risk in Iowa, Evidence Suggests
items.summary: Efforts to get rid of unstable explosives at an Iowa plant began more than a year ago but weren’t completed at that time, setting the stage for Wednesday’s controversial blast.

items.title: Trump Rejoiced in the Market’s Nvidia Surge. It Didn’t Last Long.
items.summary: The retreat of the stock market in recent days shows how President Trump’s push to reinstall the company’s chief executive has collided with the realities of his other policies.

items.title: Nvidia Halts Sales to Southeast Asia as U.S. Tightens China Restrictions
items.summary: The shipping halt, which hit four countries, follows a new U.S. rule that would require licenses for companies in the countries to buy advanced A.I. chips.

items.title: Trump’s Latest Tariffs Revive Focus on Pressuring China
items.summary: President Trump sent a message to trading partners across Asia, many of which depend on trade and investment from both the United States and China, that he is ready to escalate tariffs.

items.title: Trump Tried to Cripple Huawei. Now It Is Central to China’s A.I. Push.
items.summary: As China’s access to Nvidia’s advanced chips shrinks, Huawei is becoming increasingly indispensable to Beijing despite a wide technological gap with its American rival.

items.title: Lured by High Salaries, Some Brazilians Were Duped Into Fighting for Russia
items.summary: Dozens of Brazilians were sent to the front lines with little training, and the high salaries they were promised, they say, turned out to be illusory.

items.title: Brazilian Duped Into Fighting for Russia: ‘War Is Hell’
items.summary: Dozens of Brazilians have joined the Russian army, some say lured by a pair of recruiters promising money and adventure. Here is one soldier’s story.

items.title: Democrats Confront a Familiar Question: How Are You Going to Pay for That?
items.summary: Many Democratic plans are unlikely to become law under President Trump. But the party is still grappling with the difficult budget math of its agenda.

items.title: Congo Ebola outbreak reaches 12,000 cases as some responders evacuate
items.summary: As the fast-moving outbreak continues to spread in eastern Congo, fighting between rebels and the army is disrupting efforts to contain the spread of the disease.

items.title: North Korea's Kim vows to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring Trump's overture
items.summary: Leader Kim Jong Un reportedly visited facilities that produce nuclear ingredients and called for building more nuclear weapons to cope with threats from the U.S. and South Korea.

items.title: Storms disrupt Thanksgiving travel. And, FCC violated ABC's free speech, judge says
items.summary: The East Coast's weather is a major concern this holiday, as it could lead to coastal flooding. And, the judge says the FCC can't punish ABC for satire Trump doesn't like.

items.title: At Albuquerque's Indian Pueblo Kitchen, Native American dishes are the main course
items.summary: At an Albuquerque, N.M., museum, the restaurant is just as much of a draw as the exhibitions, with dishes like green chile stew and sweet biscochitos flavored with anise and cinnamon.

items.title: 'Memories of a Good Meal': How food made a difference during WWII
items.summary: New Orleans Chef Alon Shaya's new cookbook shares stories of resilience from World War II, centered around food.

items.title: A dish with a story, Thanksgiving with culinary historian Michael Twitty
items.summary: NPR's Leila Fadel welcomes culinary historian Michael Twitty into her kitchen for a Thanksgiving cooking session on making Kush, the forerunner to Southern cornbread dressing.

items.title: Court lets Puerto Rico governor fire firm that runs the island's troubled power grid
items.summary: LUMA Energy took over the electric grid five years ago. The court's ruling nullifies its contract, and gives the government a year to find a new operator.

items.title: Powerful storms disrupt holiday travel, as Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is postponed
items.summary: Extreme weather that has unleashed strong winds, high tides, heavy rain and floods is expected to impact travel plans of an estimated 81.5 million people as they travel across the United States.

items.title: FCC says SpaceX can deploy 1 million satellites for data centers in space. Scientists are skeptical
items.summary: The Trump administration gave Elon Musk's SpaceX the green light to deploy 1 million satellites that it said would create data centers in space, a move that has raised skepticism among scientists.

items.title: Andy Taylor, guitarist of new wave icons Duran Duran, dies at 65
items.summary: Taylor revealed his battle with Stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer in 2022. He was the guitarist of the 1980s English band Duran Duran, whose pop hits included "Hungry Like the Wolf" and "Rio".

items.title: Scattered flight delays, flooding and outages as powerful storm hits East Coast
items.summary: The Thanksgiving Day storm is progressing through the Mid-Atlantic region with high wind and flood warnings from Virginia Beach to New York City.

items.title: ICE arrests man in Boston days after he won $1 million in lottery
items.summary: “Looks like his luck ran out,” an ICE official said of Ariel Velasquez-Morales.

items.title: For a Macy’s 100th Thanksgiving parade planner, ‘there’s only one shot’
items.summary: Brendan Kennedy has spent two years preparing every detail for the milestone event, which has been postponed until Saturday due to bad weather.

items.title: First Bible published by American colonists was in Wampanoag, a Native language
items.summary: In the aftermath of war, some Puritan clerics sought new ways to convert Native Americans. They decided religious texts were the answer.

items.title: Asked about Iran-contra, Reagan joked about pardoning a turkey. A tradition followed.
items.summary: The president would have preferred to keep the focus on Hawaiian Charlie.

items.title: Tech billionaire takes his case against red tape to the Federal Reserve
items.summary: Marc Andreessen, a Trump ally whose firm has invested heavily in health care, education and housing, says he will use his role on a new Fed task force to argue that regulation is blocking progress in those sectors.

items.title: Which came first, Macy’s Thanksgiving parade or sliced bread? Take our history quiz.
items.summary: Is Harvard older than calculus? Did the Titanic sink before Oreos hit store shelves? Test your sense of history with these surprising matchups of events and inventions.

items.title: The mortality gap between Black and White Americans keeps shrinking
items.summary: The gap in the number of excess deaths between Black Americans and White Americans shrank significantly between 1993 and 2023, according to a new study.

items.title: Trump wants to work with Democrats on health care. But can they find a compromise?
items.summary: Democrats are focused on boosting Affordable Care Act subsidies and reversing Republican cuts to Medicaid, which are in opposition to Trump’s policies.

items.title: Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed by storm, rescheduled for Saturday
items.summary: A major storm is expected to hit the East Coast on Thursday.
